ops.body:
Same wrong branch, observed from the `info` side — and it cost a mis-routed release commit today.

In this colocated jj repo, `ccx vcs info` printed:

    lane        jj
    vcs         jj
    branch      main
    trunk       main

while the working copy's `@-` actually carried the bookmark `fix-gtapi-400-body` (a stale bookmark left at df3f2be, whose work was already merged to main). Acting on that `branch main` line, I ran a path-scoped `ccx vcs ship` expecting trunk. Ship then did exactly what its own rules say — appended to the checked-out bookmark — and reported `pushed fix-gtapi-400-body → origin`, creating a branch with no PR and leaving `main` untouched. `origin/main` had meanwhile advanced one commit past the base, so it wasn't even a fast-forward.

So `info` and `ship` disagree with each other on the jj lane: `info` reports what looks like the git HEAD branch, `ship` uses the bookmark at `@-`. This task covers ship misreporting where it pushed; the same resolution appears to be wrong one step earlier, in what `info` tells the operator *before* they commit. Worth fixing as one thing — `info` is the surface people check precisely to avoid this.

Recovery, for the record: `jj rebase -s <change> -d main`, `jj bookmark move main --to <change>`, restore the stale bookmark with `jj bookmark set … --allow-backwards`, `jj git push -b main`, `git push origin --delete fix-gtapi-400-body`.

Suggested acceptance criterion for whichever fix lands: on the jj lane with `@-` on a non-trunk bookmark, `ccx vcs info` names that bookmark, and it is the same name a subsequent ship reports pushing.

Observed 2026-09-03, ccx v0.56.0, jj 0.43.0.
